channel.title: Briefing
channel.description: A personal audio briefing of tech and world news.

item.title: TSA brings back gate access for some people without plane tickets 25 years after 9/11
item.description:
The Transportation Security Administration is launching a new program called Gateside by T. S. A. PreCheck. This program allows eligible members without plane tickets to pass through security and enter gate areas. This initiative brings back a pre-nine-eleven tradition that ended nearly twenty-five years ago.
The free program is initially available at thirteen airports. These include Los Angeles International Airport and Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport. They also include Harry Reid International Airport in Las Vegas and Salt Lake City International Airport. The T. S. A. plans to expand the program to additional airports in the coming months.
Interested members must apply online one to three days before their planned visits. They must receive approval before heading to the airport. Approved individuals can use a T. S. A. PreCheck lane with an acceptable form of identification.
The passes are valid for one calendar day. They allow for reentries on that same day. Members of other trusted-traveler programs who possess a Known Traveler Number are also eligible to apply.
The T. S. A. stated this initiative serves as an exclusive benefit for trusted travelers. It makes it easier to return to the gate for welcomes and send-offs. It helps people meet friends during a layover and enjoy airport dining and shopping.

item.title: Iran says it hit American vessels, oil tankers in Hormuz in retaliation for U.S. strikes
item.description:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps said they struck two American vessels and eight oil tankers in the Gulf. This was retaliation against the United States for destroying five Iranian tankers. The Guards stated the targeted vessels tried to cross a forbidden area of the Hormuz Strait.
United States Central Command reported that the American military destroyed five Iranian crude oil tankers on Tuesday. This happened after the Iranian Guard fired ballistic missiles at an American warship twice over the past two days. The targeted American warship successfully evaded the attack and no American personnel were harmed.
Central Command stated that United States forces struck four tankers in the Gulf of Oman. These were named the M T Kaviz, the M T Charminar, the M T Horizon one, and the M T Riesco. They also struck the M T Derya near Iran's Kharg Island. American forces directed the crews to abandon ship before rendering the vessels inoperable.
This exchange follows the United States military destroying three Iranian tankers on Saturday. That action was in response to the Guard firing ballistic missiles at an aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer. The escalating conflict along a critical oil corridor has pushed Brent crude to near one hundred dollars a barrel.
Iranian Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi, dismissed United States sanctions on the platform X as a rehash of a failed strategy.
In a separate incident on Tuesday, Central Command addressed an unmanned submersible that Iran reportedly seized in the Strait of Hormuz. United States Navy Captain, Tim Hawkins, stated that an underwater drone operated by United States forces malfunctioned more than a day ago while surveying regional waters. Hawkins dismissed the captured craft as an older and defective model. It carried no classified sonar or radar equipment and collected no sensitive data.
Iranian media outlets identified the sub as a Dive-L-D autonomous undersea vehicle developed by Anduril. The craft costs two point five million dollars each according to a twenty twenty-four DefenseScoop report. An Anduril spokesperson noted that the Dive-L-D is an attritable autonomous system designed to operate in dangerous environments where loss is expected.

item.title: Delhi Satya Niketan building collapse: PG operator arrested, adjacent unsafe building demolished | Top updates
item.description: Delhi Police arrested Sudhanshu. He is an operator of the Hostel Daze paying guest facility inside a five-storey building. The building in Delhi's Satya Niketan area collapsed on Sunday afternoon, September sixth, twenty twenty-five. The disaster resulted in seven fatalities, including five students. Sudhanshu and his business partner Shubham Tyagi had leased the property in August twenty twenty-five. Shubham remains at large. Police are investigating the circumstances of the collapse and the roles of those linked to the ownership, maintenance, repair work, and paying guest operations. Repair work had been underway in the building basement for eight to ten days before the collapse. Police previously arrested property owners Hariram Bansal, who is eighty-one, and his wife Urmila Gupta, who is seventy-five. They arrested their fifty-two-year-old son Mahesh Gupta as well. The older couple was placed in fourteen-day judicial custody. Mahesh was remanded to two days of police custody. Authorities also apprehended labor contractor Sanoj from Kasganj, Uttar Pradesh, who was allegedly supervising the basement repairs. A building contractor and a mason are also being produced in court. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta ordered the demolition of the adjacent dilapidated building to ensure public safety. The Delhi C. M. O. stated on X that Delhi Fire Service personnel are systematically removing students' belongings from that adjacent structure. The Supreme Court will examine the collapse on a pan-India basis. A bench of Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R. Mahadevan listed the matter for a hearing on Thursday following a mention by senior advocate and amicus curiae Ajit Sinha.

item.title: Why Nepal is demanding climate justice and compensation after deadly floods
item.description: Nepal is demanding climate justice and twenty million dollars in compensation. This follows catastrophic floods on August twenty-sixth that killed more than one thousand three hundred people. The disaster left over five thousand people missing. It was triggered when a mountain glacier collapsed. A torrent of water and mud rushed into Nepal. It hit the Rasuwa region and the Nuwakot region, as well as China. Foreign Minister, Shisir Khanal, stated that Nepal is paying the ultimate price for a global crisis. He emphasized that support should be viewed as climate justice rather than charity. President, Ramchandra Paudel, echoed this appeal in an address to the nation on Monday. Nepal observed a national day of mourning for the victims on that same day. The Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Environment wrote a joint letter to the United Nations. They requested twenty million dollars in damages. The United Nations Loss and Damage Fund faces a two point eight billion dollar funding gap. This gap exists as the fund prepares to approve its first climate recovery projects. Nepal contributes less than zero point one percent of global greenhouse gas emissions. Yet its glaciers have lost close to one-third of their volume in roughly three decades due to global warming. Preliminary estimates from the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority put property and housing and infrastructure losses at some two point five six billion dollars.

item.title: Eiffel Tower row over Hindu sect BAPS unites French politicians – but divides Indian diaspora
item.description:
The Eiffel Tower was closed on Monday after staff went on strike. Female workers were removed and replaced by men during a private tour. The tour was for a Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha delegation.
The incident united French politicians across the political spectrum in commenting on the fracas. This happened ahead of the twenty twenty-seven election. Socialist Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire promised an investigation. Île-de-France president Valérie Pécresse expressed shock. Far-right leader Marine Le Pen stated that France would never accept that the presence of women be limited.
Progressive diaspora Indians had held a public meeting on Saturday to raise awareness. They talked about the sect's conservative and misogynistic practices and ties to Hindu nationalism. They warned that the Eiffel Tower story must not become fodder for more racism and far-right backlash.
B. A. P. S. released a statement apologizing for any pain or inconvenience. They noted that to their knowledge access to the monument was never denied to anyone.
Indian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal called the matter purely between the concerned entities.
The B. A. P. S. Hindu sect inaugurated Europe's largest traditional temple on Sunday. It is located in Bussy-Saint-Georges, a Paris suburb. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi delivered a virtual message. He hailed the new temple as a symbol of bilateral cooperation.

item.title: US Open 2026 quarter-final: Ben Shelton v Carlos Alcaraz goes to final set – live
item.description:
At two fifty-one a.m. during the U. S. Open quarter-final at Arthur Ashe Stadium, Ben Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz pushed their match past the previous tournament record for a latest finish.
The previous record had been set at two fifty a.m. by Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner during their twenty twenty-two quarter-final.
Carlos Alcaraz won that twenty twenty-two match six to three, six to seven, six to seven, seven to five, and six to three after five hours and fifteen minutes.
The current match advanced to a fifth and deciding set after Shelton claimed the third set and Alcaraz fought back.
Earlier in the contest, Alcaraz secured the opening set six to three in a sixty-one-minute battle that included a first-set tiebreak.
Shelton subsequently claimed the second set in forty-nine minutes, leveling the match at one set apiece, before taking the third set in forty-eight minutes.
Alcaraz then forced the fifth set, with his performance featuring thirty-seven unforced errors through the early stages of the match and a first-serve percentage that dipped to fifty percent in the second set.
Shelton relied heavily on a powerful serve that topped out at one hundred forty-nine miles per hour and reached speeds of one hundred forty-four miles per hour and one hundred forty-two miles per hour at critical moments.
Shelton also won sixty-eight percent of his first-serve points and converted key break opportunities against the Spaniard.

item.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay to travel to London on first official overseas visit; gold ring scheme launch postponed
item.description:
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay will take his first official overseas trip on Thursday, September tenth, twenty twenty-six. He is traveling to London to attract investments and meet with entrepreneurs and industrialists.
Mister Vijay leaves from Chennai airport on the night of September tenth and arrives in London on September eleventh. His return to Chennai is planned for the morning of September seventeenth.
During his week-long United Kingdom trip, he will highlight the state investment potential. Officials expect him to witness the signing of important memoranda of understanding between the Tamil Nadu government and multinational companies.
This follows the recent Vettri Tamil Nadu Investors Conclave. That event secured agreements with ninety-seven companies for investments worth sixty-seven thousand four hundred and eighty-two crore rupees.
The Chief Minister will also tour motorsport facilities and a circuit in London. This follows his recent assembly announcement to build a motorsport city in Tamil Nadu.
He will hold discussions with members of the Tamil diaspora during the journey. Secretaries one and four will accompany him along with senior officials of Guidance Tamil Nadu.
Sources confirmed his schedule remains unchanged despite reports of a proposed visit by Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim to Chennai. Because of this trip, the launch of the T. V. K. government welfare scheme named Thaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam has been postponed. It was originally set to launch on September fifteenth, twenty twenty-six. Additional events tied to party figures Annadurai and Ramasamy are also likely to be postponed.

item.title: BRICS leaders gather in India, but does the group have a clear purpose?
item.description:
India is hosting the eighteenth B. R. I. C. S. summit in Delhi this weekend. The slogan is Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. This reinterprets the original acronym for the five founding members of Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa. It now includes new members Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates. The bloc now represents nearly half the world population and about forty percent of global G. D. P.
Mihaela Papa, director of the B. R. I. C. S. Lab at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, noted that India adds clout. It has significant geopolitical weight and relationships across competing camps. This makes it an important bridge builder.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian will attend. United Arab Emirates President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan is expected to send representatives. Saudi Arabia is also expected to attend even though its B. R. I. C. S. status remains somewhat ambiguous.
For host India, the summit serves as a platform for bilateral meetings. This includes a scheduled Friday meeting between Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. It is also an opportunity for Modi and Xi to speak face to face amid continued strain in the China and India relationship.
Yale University lecturer Sushant Singh stated that concrete outcomes and what is achievable will likely be very limited. B. R. I. C. S. is simply not a priority for India. India is not comfortable with any kind of anti-western line. It focuses instead on defense ties with the U. S. and trade ties with the west as a whole.
Papa expects progress this weekend specifically in trade and agriculture. Progress will also involve monetary cooperation using an alternative financial architecture for currency exchange. She noted that India is keen for a coordinated approach from B. R. I. C. S. to trade and the World Trade Organization.
However, Singh maintains that internal contradictions will continue to make consensus difficult. These include a growing number of autocracies and tense bilateral relations among members.

item.title: Family of British man found dead in Grenada ask local police to work with UK investigators
item.description:
The family of forty-seven-year-old British father Andrew Frederick is urging local authorities to cooperate with United Kingdom investigators. Frederick was found dead in Grenada on the fourth of January. His body was discovered at his rental property. A privately hired pathologist concluded that week that he was a victim of homicide. In June, the director of public prosecution in Grenada, Howard Pinnock, stated there was no basis to treat the case as a homicide. He added that it would be sent to the coroner.
After a sustained campaign by the family, British authorities became involved. The body of Frederick was repatriated to the United Kingdom last month. A second autopsy revealed his organs were missing. The United Kingdom coroner recorded his cause of death as unascertained. Last week at the West London coroner court, senior coroner Lydia Brown suspended the inquest. This happened after the Metropolitan Police launched a criminal investigation. No arrests have been made. Officers from the Metropolitan Police have contacted the Royal Grenada Police Force to offer assistance.
In a statement to the Guardian, the family said justice for Andrew depends on everyone with the power to act on both sides of the Atlantic doing what is right. They are calling on Grenadian authorities to share information and collaborate with the Metropolitan Police. They are also seeking answers regarding the absence of the organs of Frederick. The Office of the Commissioner in Grenada stated that the matter will progress to the coroner court for the parish of Saint George.

item.title: Interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS is bursting with methanol
item.description:
On September ninth, twenty twenty-six, the National Radio Astronomy Observatory announced a major discovery. Observations from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array show that interstellar comet three I slash ATLAS contains exceptionally high levels of methanol.
Researchers observed the comet using the Atacama Compact Array as it moved closer to the Sun. Sunlight heated the icy surface of the comet. Scientists concentrated on the submillimeter signatures of methanol and hydrogen cyanide. They measured methanol-to-H. C. N. ratios of roughly seventy and one hundred twenty on two observation dates. These values place three I slash ATLAS among the most methanol-rich comets ever studied. Its abundance exceeds almost all known comets from our own solar system.
Lead author of the research is, Nathan Roth, a professor with American University. He shared that observing three I slash ATLAS is like taking a fingerprint from another solar system. He noted that the details reveal what it is made of. He added that it is bursting with methanol in a way we just do not usually see in comets in our own solar system.
Earlier observations with the James Webb Space Telescope had already found a coma dominated by carbon dioxide while the comet was still far from the Sun. The new A. L. M. A. data revealed more secrets. Hydrogen cyanide originates mostly from the central nucleus of the comet. Methanol comes from both the nucleus and tiny icy grains floating within the coma.
Temperatures rise and these small grains act like miniature comets. They release additional methanol into the surrounding gas and dust. This marks the first time researchers have traced the detailed physics of this type of outgassing in an interstellar object.
Comet three I slash ATLAS is only the third confirmed object ever observed entering our solar system from interstellar space. It follows one I slash 'Oumuamua and two I slash Borisov.
The measurements suggest that the ice inside three I slash ATLAS formed under very different conditions. Or it was exposed to conditions that shaped most comets in our solar system differently. This offers new insight into how small icy bodies form in other planetary systems.

item.title: Batteries just broke another record in the US
item.description: Battery installations in the United States reached a record twenty point two gigawatt hours of new capacity in the second quarter of twenty twenty-six. This comes from a report by Benchmark Mineral Intelligence and the Solar Energy Industries Association. That capacity supplies the daily electricity needs of about seven hundred thousand homes. The surge puts the country on a trajectory to install seventy-one gigawatt hours of batteries this year. That is a twenty percent increase over last year. Cheaper batteries and the need for storage are driving this growth as solar and wind power join the grid. Massive utility scale systems drove the record quarter. This includes seven new gigascale installations with a capacity of over one gigawatt hour each. Shan Tomouk, energy storage and energy lead for Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, stated that it really came down to a handful of big projects. Behind the meter batteries also grew. Data centers led the commercial sector by making up about three quarters of new batteries. Residential batteries saw a sharp slowdown. Home installations are projected to drop by sixteen percent in twenty twenty-six compared to last year. Tomouk noted that this drop happened largely because a tax credit subsidizing home battery systems ended in twenty twenty-five. Home installations should recover by the end of the decade, and nonresidential tax credits have largely survived. Isshu Kikuma, an energy storage analyst at BloombergNEF, described the sector as one of the strong spots in United States energy right now. Nearly all the systems coming online use cells made in China.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine exchange strikes as two killed at Moldova border
item.description: Two people were killed when Russian drones struck the Starokozache border crossing between Ukraine and Moldova. The strike forced the facility to close. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that the aggression must be stopped here and now before it spreads any further. The overnight attack also injured three people, including a Moldovan driver. This was reported by Odesa regional head Oleh Kiper and the foreign ministry of Moldova. In the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv, a woman was killed and fourteen people were injured. That total includes two children after a Russian drone hit a nine storey residential building. In Russia, officials reported that four people were killed and twenty-nine others injured in a Ukrainian drone attack. The strike happened in the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk. Governor Veniamin Kondratiev described it as a massive overnight enemy drone attack. A child was among those killed in that port city. A drone also hit an industrial facility in the Arctic city of Novy Urengoy. That location is nearly three thousand kilometres from Ukraine. Falling wreckage triggered a fire there with no injuries reported, according to regional governor Dmitry Artyukhov. The defence ministry of Russia stated its forces shot down five hundred ninety-six Ukrainian drones overnight. The cross-border strikes occurred as Russia and Ukraine stepped up long-range attacks. This happened despite renewed diplomatic efforts following a phone call between Russian President Vladimir Putin and United States President Donald Trump about ending the war. Weekend meetings also took place in Moscow and Kyiv involving United States envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff.

item.title: The Download: OpenAI’s turning point for math and a battery record
item.description: OpenAI states its agents solved the Navier-Stokes equations. This was a ninety-year-old mathematics problem. It took eighty-eight hours and ten thousand A. I. agents. The achievement involved spending millions of dollars to win a one million dollar math contest. It marks what OpenAI claims is the first major math problem solved by artificial intelligence. However, the announcement has been overshadowed by accusations. Critics say OpenAI failed to credit researchers whose A. I.-assisted work influenced the solution. Meanwhile, United States battery installations reached a record twenty point two gigawatt-hours of new capacity in the second quarter of twenty twenty-six. This is enough to supply the daily electricity needs of six hundred thousand homes. The surge places the country on track for another record year. It is driven by cheaper batteries and rising energy storage demands from grid renewables. Danijar Hafner is developing A. I. agents. These agents are capable of planning ahead and navigating unfamiliar environments. The United States accused six Chinese A. I. firms of industrial-scale theft. These firms include DeepSeek and Alibaba. Apple is expected to unveil a folding smartphone priced at two thousand dollars. Meta also launched an A. I. agent named Muse. Muse is capable of accessing apps to send emails and make payments. Internal tests showed it could expose sensitive personal data.

item.title: New satellite images show major construction surge at Iran’s Pickaxe nuke site
item.description:
Satellite imagery reviewed by C. N. N. reveals a sharp surge in construction activity in twenty twenty-six at Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain site. This suspected nuclear facility is buried beneath a granite mountain near the Natanz complex about one hundred forty miles south of Tehran.
The analysis was conducted by the Center for Strategic and International Studies and is based on six years of imagery. It shows the site has shifted from active excavation toward internal construction. There is also exterior reinforcement, road paving, and hardening of tunnel portal accesses.
Analysts indicated the facility is likely designed as a safe haven or housing for Iran's nuclear programme. It could serve as a potential centrifuge assembly plant, an enrichment facility, or a location for uranium metal conversion. However, it is not yet capable of enrichment work.
U. S. President Donald Trump has repeatedly threatened to strike the heavily fortified location. He stated last week that they may hit Pickaxe very soon. He also noted that they know everyone moving at the site.
The U. S. military maintains operational plans for strikes against Pickaxe Mountain using some of the largest bombs in its arsenal. The granite mountain presents a difficult target. A defence agency signed an emergency one point two million dollar contract justification for a subterranean test facility. Meanwhile, the U. S. military is currently developing a next generation penetrator bomb to reach deeply buried targets.

item.title: A Stealth Startup Thinks It Just Hacked the Memory Shortage
item.description:
San Jose startup Kepler Computing has emerged from seven years in stealth mode. It has raised four hundred sixty-eight million dollars in funding. The United States Department of Commerce committed up to two hundred forty-five million dollars in July.
Physicists and computer scientists founded the company in twenty eighteen. They developed a three dimensional stacking approach and a proprietary material. This technology handles high bandwidth memory and high speed cache memory. It completely bypasses expensive extreme ultraviolet lithography.
The startup technology increases density without extreme ultraviolet equipment. It works directly inside existing semiconductor fabrication plants. A factory can convert its lines in eight months instead of the typical twenty-four months.
Kepler raised capital from several major backers. Investors include GlobalFoundries, Intel Capital, AMD Ventures, Baillie Gifford, and Bill Gates through Gates Frontier.
The company partnered directly with GlobalFoundries. That partner invested fifty million dollars. GlobalFoundries also hosts testing at facilities in Singapore and Burlington, Vermont.
Kepler plans to ship its first high bandwidth memory chip samples later this year. The company will ramp up production in Singapore next year. United States chip production will begin in twenty twenty-eight. The startup has already run its technology on roughly two thousand wafers to date.
Chief executive officer Debo Olaosebikan explained the strategy. He said the team originally planned to work on static random-access memory first. Dynamic random-access memory and high bandwidth memory would follow later.
The launch of ChatGPT changed everything. The explosion of demand for alternative memory forced a shift in the road map. Now the company is making static random-access memory and high bandwidth memory at the same time.
The new approach aims to ease the global memory chip shortage. Manufacturers can increase memory supply within existing facilities. This avoids the twenty billion to forty billion dollar cost of building brand new plants. Success depends on the startup scaling its technology to millions of devices.

item.title: NASA Names Two Artemis II Astronauts to Emeritus Program
item.description:
National Aeronautics and Space Administration astronauts Victor Glover and Reid Wiseman are moving to emeritus status in September twenty twenty-six. This happens after their Artemis Two mission at the Johnson Space Center in Houston. The emeritus role lets experts donate time to train and mentor current workers. They keep the freedom to pursue other opportunities.
Victor Glover was the pilot for Artemis Two. Reid Wiseman commanded the mission after spending one hundred sixty-five days aboard the International Space Station. They were two of four astronauts to launch on top of the Space Launch System rocket. They flew inside the Orion spacecraft for a mission around the Moon. They splashed down on April tenth as part of the first human crew to travel to lunar orbit in more than fifty years.
Both astronauts will share their expertise with flight controllers and engineers in their new roles. This happens as the agency prepares for Artemis Three and the Artemis Four mission in twenty twenty-eight.
National Aeronautics and Space Administration Administrator Jared Isaacman shared his thoughts. He is grateful they will continue sharing what they learned with the team as they prepare for Artemis Three in twenty twenty-seven and the missions that follow.

item.title: Shopify acquires Tailwind
item.description: Shopify has acquired the Tailwind C. S. S. framework. The tool was launched over nine years ago. It is currently installed more than one hundred ten million times per week. Companies like C. H. A. T. G. P. T., X, Cloudflare, Reddit, and Shopify use it. Tailwind states that Shopify was one of the very first companies operating at scale to adopt the framework for itself and its customers. The announcement states that nothing will change regarding the framework. It and other open-source projects will remain M. I. T. licensed. The existing team will lead them with support from Shopify. On the commercial side, sign-ups for new customers are closing now. All existing customers will maintain access to products like Tailwind Plus and U. I. dot s. h. The acquisition gives Tailwind a stable long-term home. It will be actively maintained and developed to serve a real product at Shopify. This addresses the needs of merchants, custom storefront design, admin management, and checkout experiences. Additionally, Shopify explores agentic commerce. The creator notes that entrepreneurship changed their life and expresses belief in Shopify's mission to empower entrepreneurs.

item.title: Scientists find a bone-building switch that could fight osteoporosis
item.description:
Researchers at Leipzig University have identified a cell surface receptor called G. P. R. one thirty-three. It plays a key role in regulating bone health and points to a new treatment for osteoporosis. The findings were published on September ninth, twenty twenty-six. In Germany alone, osteoporosis affects about six million people. Most of those people are women.
G. P. R. one thirty-three is an adhesion G. protein-coupled receptor. It responds to physical forces and cellular interactions inside bone tissue. When activated, the receptor shifts the biological balance. It encourages bone-forming cells called osteoblasts. It also reduces the activity of bone-resorbing cells called osteoclasts.
Researchers used an experimental compound called A. P. five oh three. They found it via a computer-assisted screen to stimulate G. P. R. one thirty-three. The research team significantly increased bone strength in healthy mice and mice with osteoporosis-like bone loss. If this receptor is impaired by genetic changes, mice show early signs of bone density loss. This loss is similar to human osteoporosis. Lead investigator Professor, Ines Liebscher from the Rudolf Schönheimer Institute of Biochemistry noted that using A. P. five oh three successfully increased bone strength across the test subjects.
An earlier study found that A. P. five oh three activation also strengthens skeletal muscle. Because of this, the compound holds potential for combating age-related decline in an aging population. Lead author Doctor, Juliane Lehmann stated that the parallel strengthening of bone and muscle highlights the medical potential of the receptor. A treatment improving both tissues could help older adults maintain mobility and stability. It would also reduce fracture risks. The Leipzig team is now pursuing follow-up projects to understand G. P. R. one thirty-three more fully. They will also investigate potential applications in other diseases.

item.title: NOAA is putting commercial fishing ahead of conservation
item.description: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration announced new agency priorities last week. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration stated the changes aim to cut bureaucracy, modernize science, and prioritize fishing communities. The reforms serve as an operational roadmap to fulfill the executive order signed by President Donald Trump in April twenty twenty-five. The order is called Restoring American Seafood Competitiveness. Experts state that the actions will erode fish stocks, threaten endangered species, and surrender marine habitats to destructive trawlers. In July, the administration relegated endangered leatherback turtles, sea lions, and whales to collateral damage. The changes follow letters sent to regional fisheries councils earlier in the summer. Those letters directed councils to dismantle restrictions in favor of more permissive fishing procedures. The agency plans to open marine national monuments to commercial fishing operations. It will scale back critical habitat designations to focus on the downstream economics of conservation. It will also weaken decades of peer-reviewed science. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration is often called N O O A. Andrea Treece criticized the direction in an email to Inside Climate News. She is a senior attorney in the Oceans Program at Earthjustice. She stated that if you asked A I to come up with a plan to hollow out marine ecosystems and impoverish coastal communities, it would look like this plan. She added that the agency is taking a sharp turn away from science. Treece also stated that it is inexcusable to make it easier to destroy marine habitats and commit endangered species to extinction for short-term profits. Treece additionally stated that you cannot just eliminate parts of the ecosystem you find inconvenient and expect that system to continue to sustain us.

item.title: Ben Shelton wins a night of vomit, sweat and home hopes to triumph at US Open
item.description: Ben Shelton defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in a five-set quarter-final at the United States Open. The epic win started on Tuesday night and concluded on Wednesday morning. Ben Shelton fired seven aces during the grueling encounter to secure his historic tournament triumph. The match ended at three thirty-three a.m. at the Arthur Ashe Stadium. This marked the latest-ever finish at the tournament and the fifth-latest finish in grand slam history. Soccer star Trinity Rodman and Shelton's mother and sister watched the late-night match from the stands. The victory keeps alive a real chance of an American man winning the tournament for the first time since two thousand three.

item.title: What next for LIV Golf's star players, and its fight for survival?
item.description: L. I. V. Golf filed for bankruptcy protection in the United States on Tuesday. The league wants to restructure for a new era next year. This leaves the league owing at least forty-five million dollars to fourteen current and former players. Court documents show the breakaway league estimates its assets at one hundred million to five hundred million dollars. Its liabilities are listed at between five hundred million dollars and one billion dollars. This follows an outlay of five billion dollars that split professional golf after its launch in twenty twenty-one. Star players can now opt to leave rather than being obliged to see out their contracts in the new version of the league. Bryson DeChambeau and Cameron Smith are among those who previously rejected returning player deals to stay on. This new version aims to launch next year with a scaled-back business model. It will feature tournaments worth around seven million pounds. It will also feature expanded fields from fifty-seven to seventy-five players along with Monday qualifying events and halfway cuts. In response to the filing, the D. P. World Tour stated it has had a high volume of inbound interest from L. I. V. players. The tour is exploring ways to accommodate those who leave. Players must be free from third-party contractual restrictions and abide by membership regulations. A spokesperson for the D. P. World Tour said their tournament committee has approved the process. Returning to the mainstream tours remains complicated. Brooks Koepka previously quit L. I. V. in December twenty twenty-five. He returned to the P. G. A. Tour in twenty twenty-six after making a five million dollar charitable donation. He also gave up FedEx Cup bonus scheme payments. He accepted ineligibility for the player equity programme until twenty thirty. The P. G. A. Tour described this as one of the largest financial repercussions in professional sports history. However, P. G. A. Tour Chief Executive Officer Brian Rolapp indicated last month there are no current plans to run that returning member programme again. Other players like Patrick Reed have had to earn their place back through the D. P. World Tour Race to Dubai top ten. Jon Rahm said this week he was prepared to fulfil his contract with the first version of L. I. V. He made no mention of any commitment to the intended new iteration. He is expected to depart alongside other players seeking a way back to the mainstream circuits.

item.title: Torrential rains, winds from Hurricane Lowell leaves 30,000 without power
item.description:
Hurricane Lowell brought heavy rains and strong winds to the Hawaiian island of Kauai. Thirty thousand residents were left without power. The category one hurricane did not make landfall on the island. It caused massive destruction from one hundred twenty-eight kilometres west of the island. This was reported by the Hawaii County Civil Defense Agency. By early Tuesday nearly ninety-two percent of Kauai Island Utility Cooperative residents lost power.
The storm flooded coastal roads and washed away sections of beachside roads. Roughly three hundred residents were forced to evacuate. Emergency officials asked residents to conserve water. They urged people to stay off the roads and shelter in place. Crews are now clearing debris and assessing the damage. Hawaiian mayor, Derek Kawakami reported extensive damage on Tuesday. He stated that everyone is now gathering data and information.
The storm center passed west of the islands overnight and moved north. The National Hurricane Center warned that flooding and mudslides remain a risk. By late Tuesday morning maximum sustained winds decreased to near sixty-five miles per hour. There were higher gusts as the storm moved north at fourteen miles per hour. Hurricane warnings for Kauai and Niihau were lifted by Tuesday morning. A tropical storm warning for Oahu was also lifted. High surf and deadly rip currents will continue to affect exposed coasts for another day or two.

item.title: What Is Math’s Mysterious Langlands Program Really About?
item.description:
The Langlands program is a decades long mathematical effort. It was launched in nineteen sixty-seven by Canadian mathematician Robert Langlands in a letter to a colleague. The project explores unexpected wormhole like connections between distant realms of mathematics. It links number theory with harmonic analysis. Number theory studies numbers and polynomial equations. Harmonic analysis examines signals and waves and modular forms.
At the heart of the project are profound correspondences between different mathematical objects. Solutions to the polynomial equation x cubed minus two equals zero generate an extended number field. This field has an associated Galois group of symmetries called S three. These symmetries can be expressed as two by two matrices. The Langlands correspondence shows that the matrix traces match coefficients of prime numbered powers in a specific modular form.
Hundreds of mathematicians have spent decades trying to extend and exploit these bridges between disparate fields. Expert David Ben Zvi of the University of Texas at Austin noted the breadth of the project. He stated that everyone has heard of it. He also noted that experts generally lack a complete understanding of what the program truly is.
The program is often called a grand unified theory of mathematics. It suggests an underlying unity to the mathematical universe. Its specific correspondences remain excruciatingly specific and esoteric and not yet fully mined for their deepest meaning.

item.title: Denisovan tools from cave in China shows how mysterious humans lived
item.description:
Researchers discovered Denisovan fossils and stone tools inside Bianfu cave in Yunnan province, China. They unearthed over sixty-four thousand bone fragments and one thousand three hundred sixty-six stone artefacts. The discovered Denisovan bones and teeth have been accurately dated between one hundred thirty-four thousand and one hundred sixty-seven thousand years old.
Molecular analysis of proteins extracted from five specimens confirmed they belonged to Denisovans. These specimens were two teeth and three bones. They contained protein variants unique to the group without any specific to H. sapiens or Neanderthals. The teeth and bones came from at least four individuals.
Researcher, Bence Viola noted this site is only the third Denisovan locale with human remains, lithics, fauna, and environmental context. The stone tools included scrapers, choppers, and one hundred thirty-five flakes. These tools were relatively simple compared with those made by Neanderthals living elsewhere in Eurasia at the same time.
The site yielded one thousand six hundred fifty-four identifiable animal bones showing butchery marks. These bones came predominantly from deer and bovids in prime condition, along with rhinoceroses, hyenas, and bamboo rats. Pollen evidence indicates the area was a mix of conifer forest and steppe with a temperate climate.
For the first time, we can know their technology and subsistence strategy. Archaeologist, Hao Li at the Institute of Tibetan Plateau Research in Beijing noted this milestone.

item.title: ChatGPT 1980s photo trend: What happens to your picture after you upload it?
item.description:
A viral chat g p t trend turns selfies into nineteen eighties style photos. This trend raises privacy questions about how personal images and data are handled.
According to wired middle east, uploading a photo puts personal identifying data onto an A. I. service. The data includes metadata like when the picture was taken, the device used, and its location.
The uploaded photo becomes part of the user interaction and gets stored with conversation data. Chat g p t conversations stay on a user account until the user deletes them. Data can stay on open a i systems for up to thirty days after deletion.
Certain information can be kept longer for legal or security reasons. Information can also be kept if it is de-identified and separated from the account.
Open a i states that its business products and a p i do not use customer data for model training by default. Data handling rules for personal accounts are different.
Services can collect basic metadata. This includes I. P. addresses, device types, operating systems, and general geographic locations.
Users should avoid uploading photos of other people, especially children, without permission. Media reports recommend turning off model training where possible. Users should also use temporary or incognito modes, and delete unnecessary chats and files to protect their privacy.

item.title: Viral AI assistant Instinct now has its own email address
item.description:
The artificial intelligence assistant named Instinct, currently valued at two point five billion dollars, is rolling out dedicated email addresses for all users. This allows the autonomous agent to create and run its own accounts without cluttering human inboxes.
Founder, Noah Shinn announced the feature on Tuesday. He explained that the email addresses will let Instinct handle tasks requiring email verification. These tasks include signing up for services, contacting businesses, and following up on matters that need attention.
As, Shinn wrote on the social network X, Instinct can use its own email to contact a restaurant about a special request. It can also ask a business about availability or sign up for a service it needs to complete a task.
Users can forward order confirmations to their Instinct address so the assistant can handle product returns. People can also add the bot to group threads to track information and answer questions about pending decisions and due dates.
The earliest users already have reserved email addresses. Other people can claim theirs at mail dot instinct dot com.
This update follows a partnership with Stripe in August to enable agent purchases. It also follows a collaboration with the company, One Password last week to help manage user logins.

item.title: France's far-right National Rally fires policeman from security team over racist, sexist comments
item.description:
France's far-right National Rally party has expelled a policeman from its security team. Bodycam footage published on Tuesday in the local daily Midi Libre revealed him making racist, homophobic, and sexist remarks. The footage, dated November of last year, captures the officer and colleagues in the southern town of Carcassonne using derogatory terms while on duty.
The National Rally denounced the remarks on Wednesday as criminally punishable and entirely at odds with party values. The party stated it immediately removed the officer from its security detail and expelled him from the party. The Carcassonne prosecutor's office has launched an investigation into the incident.
The controversy poses a challenge to party leader Marine Le Pen ahead of next year's presidential election. She is working to soften the image of the anti-immigration party inherited from her father. Le Pen is running for president for a fourth time and currently leads polls in the first round of voting next spring.
President Emmanuel Macron's equality minister, Aurore Bergé, condemned the remarks as absolutely unacceptable. Former prime minister and presidential candidate, Gabriel Attal, shared the video on the social network formerly known as Twitter. He wrote that it depicts what a France led by the National Rally would look like.

item.title: Ethiopia's constitutional reform: What does it mean — especially for Abiy?
item.description:
Four thousand delegates met in Addis Ababa for weeks of national consultations. They recommended merging the offices of Ethiopia's prime minister and president into a single system. The plan creates a stronger presidential government.
Abiy Ahmed did not attend these meetings. He and his party could still benefit from the endorsement. He won a massive majority in parliamentary elections in June. That victory helps him advocate for broader executive powers.
Supporters argue a directly elected president represents the entire country. They believe this leader could unite an ethnically and regionally fragmented society.
Civil rights activist, Befeqadu Hailu, warned about the risks. He said presidential systems are more prone to descending into dictatorship. He noted that the current parliament lacks broad popular legitimacy despite having procedural power.
Opposition parties and influential armed groups boycotted the dialogue process. British journalist, Martin Plaut, described the initiative as a rubber-stamping exercise for the prime minister. He added that the reform formalizes power held since twenty eighteen.
Plaut views the structural change as a superficial fix. The plan fails to address underlying armed conflicts in Oromia and Amhara. It ignores unresolved issues from the Tigray war. It also leaves persistent tensions between the central government and more than eighty ethnic groups.

item.title: Physics-aware benchmark reveals why similar materials AI models can predict thermal conductivity differently
item.description:
Researchers have published a new physics-aware benchmark in Nature Communications. The work evaluates machine learning models predicting the thermal and mechanical properties of materials. The lead researcher is, Michele Simoncelli, an assistant professor of applied physics at Columbia. Colleagues from the University of Cambridge also helped develop the project. Those researchers are, Balázs Póta, Paramvir Ahlawat, and, Gábor Csányi.
The benchmark addresses a major flaw in machine-learning interatomic potentials. These models can run one thousand times faster than traditional approaches. They achieve this speed by bypassing explicit solutions to the Schrödinger equation.
As Simoncelli stated, an atomistic model is physics-aware only when it correctly describes atomistic physics. It must predict macroscopic properties as a direct consequence of that accurate description.
Many models show similar accuracy in predicting energy and crystal stability. However, the researchers found that these models distort the small and fast quantum-mechanical thermal vibrations of atoms. Sometimes they predict macroscopic thermal conductivity accurately only because microscopic errors accidentally cancel out.
First author, Balázs Póta, explained that models were previously compared mainly on energy performance. This previous method missed potential errors in forces that determine atomic dynamics.
The benchmarking effort began about two years ago. It compared several models against traditional quantum-mechanical calculations. The test used a set of more than one hundred crystalline materials.
The benchmark has already been adopted by several research groups and companies. These include Meta, Microsoft, Radical A. I., and Orbital Materials. The test has also been incorporated into the Matbench Discovery leaderboard.
This adoption matters because thermal management is critical for many advanced technologies. These include microchips, batteries, quantum computers, jet engines, spacecraft heat shields, and nuclear reactors. Models that get underlying physics wrong can discard good material options and promote bad ones.

item.title: Manohar asks Jana Sena cadre to prepare for local body elections in Andhra Pradesh
item.description: Nadendla Manohar urged Jana Sena party workers on Wednesday to get ready for local body elections. He spoke at the final session of an awareness program held by the party. item.title: Treasury Department to buy back up to $6 billion in longer-term debt, triple the normal level
item.description:
The Treasury Department will buy back up to six billion dollars of government debt in an operation on Thursday. The twenty minute window concludes at two p.m. E. T. This triples the normal two billion dollar buyback operation for already issued securities. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated on August nineteenth that the department would at least double the normal amount. Future operations will be at least four billion dollars.
The measure targets ten and twenty year notes to keep government debt markets liquid. It attempts to put a lid on Treasury yields that hit highs not seen since before the two thousand eight global financial crisis. Market reaction was negative. Treasury yields rose further and remained volatile. Long dated securities rose as much as five basis points each before easing. The benchmark ten year issue hit four point eight four one percent around eleven thirty a.m. E. T. The twenty year climbed to five point three one four percent. The thirty year bond rose five basis points to five point three zero seven percent.
Higher yields have coincided with government debt passing forty trillion dollars. Other factors include inflation fears from tariffs and the Iran war. Crude oil has also topped one hundred dollars a barrel. Publicly held debt sits at thirty one point eight trillion dollars. That is up eight point two percent. Treasury issuance jumped eleven point eight percent from twenty twenty-five.
The move drew criticism for breaking predictable Treasury processes. It also failed to match speculation that buybacks could reach up to ten billion dollars. Bond fund manager, Mark Spindel, is the chief investment officer at Potomac River Capital. He said this is not Hank Paulson's bazooka. He also noted that crisis required an act of Congress. Stanley Druckenmiller, head of Duquesne Family Office, criticized the defense of prices in a Wall Street Journal op-ed. He wrote that once markets believe Treasury is defending a price, every rise in yields becomes a test of official resolve. He added that operations must grow to survive the tests.

item.title: IBM releases SOTA Granite Time Series PatchTST-FM-r2 model with commercial-friendly license
item.description:
International Business Machines has released a new time-series foundation model. It is called Granite Time Series Patch-T-S-T-F-M-r-two. The model has roughly three hundred eighty-five million parameters. It features an updated architecture and a larger pretraining corpus. It also supports probabilistic forecasting and missing-value imputation.
As of September eighth, twenty twenty-six, the model ranks second overall among replicable zero-shot models on the G-I-F-T-Eval benchmark. It is also the top-performing zero-shot model under a permissive, commercial-friendly open-source license.
The model is dual-licensed under Apache two point zero and Open-M-D-W one point zero. It achieves a geometric-mean C-R-P-S of zero point four six seven. It also achieves a geometric-mean M-A-S-E of zero point six eight four six.
Architectural changes include a transition from standard transformer layers to conformer layers. These combine multi-head self-attention with temporal convolution. They also include fifty percent overlapping patches with Hamming-window weighting and overlap-and-add forecasting. The model supports context lengths of up to eight thousand one hundred ninety-two steps. It predicts ninety-nine quantiles.
The pretraining corpus consists of selected datasets from Gift-Eval-Pretrain. It includes custom synthetic data based on Kernel-Synth with modified periodic kernels. It also features a T-S-Mixup corpus. Finally, it includes approximately five hundred thousand synthetic Cau-Ker sequences of length four thousand ninety-six.
Model weights, architecture, inference pipeline, and reproduction code are available on Hugging Face and GitHub.

item.title: Recreating a 70-year love story frame by frame
item.description:
The new documentary short Love Rendered explores memory loss and the power of storytelling. The film follows Burt and Ethelle Shatz as they navigate cognitive decline. They have been married for over seventy years. Machine learning was used as a tool to guide them back through time and hold onto a vanishing moment. The film focuses on recreating an unrecorded memory from the day they met at a student co-op in Cleveland. That memory previously existed only in their minds.
The documentary was directed by Academy Award nominated filmmaker, Liz Garbus. It was produced alongside Dan Cogan and Darren Aronofsky. This was a collaboration between Google DeepMind and Aronofsky's creative venture, Primordial Soup. Google DeepMind is spelled G. O. O. G. L. E. D. E. E. P. M. I. N. D.
To reconstruct the unphotographed day, Ethelle worked with the technical team as an active co-creator. She corrected details like the curve of a staircase or the shape of a shoe heel. Engineers used generative models to restore black-and-white photos of the couple from their youth. They also used performance capture models to map Burt and Ethelle's present-day micro-mannerisms onto their younger likenesses. This included the specific tilt of Burt's head and the subtle crinkle around his eyes. As Darren noted during production, a tool does nothing until it is guided by human hands.

item.title: Get ready for the game with new football features in Search
item.description:
Football season is here. Google Search now offers new upgrades to serve as your ultimate game day guide. You get a live game feed, detailed player and league stats, and fantasy account integration.
To find the live game feed, search for an ongoing game and look for the red live icon. It gives you a recap and a dynamic timeline with play by play updates. You also get social commentary, video highlights, and artificial intelligence powered insights.

item.title: Google's AI genome system evaluates every possible one-base change
item.description: Google announced a new resource on Tuesday called AlphaGenome Atlas. It predicts the consequences of every possible single-base variant in the human genome. The system processes nine billion bases through AlphaGenome software across the human genome. The system is engineered to identify the potential functions of non-coding DNA. This non-coding material makes up the vast majority of the human genome. It does not encode proteins itself. This region does not build proteins. Portions of it are essential for controlling the activity of protein-coding regions. It instructs cells where and when to make messenger RNAs and how to process them. Much of it appears to consist of remnants from viruses and other molecular parasites. Having all this analysis performed by a single software package is useful. Being able to pinpoint functional portions of DNA is also useful. The true value of AlphaGenome will remain unclear until biologists begin heavy adoption. This adoption will show what the tool offers beyond its original training data.

item.title: Paul Christiano joins OpenAI Foundation Board
item.description: Paul Christiano is joining the OpenAI Foundation Board as a non voting observer. He will also serve as a non voting observer on the OpenAI Group P. B. C. Board. Standards and Innovation. This is within the National Institute of Standards and Technology. This agency belongs to the United States Department of Commerce. He serves there as a Senior Tech Advisor. item.title: iPhone Duo

Apple has announced the iPhone Duo, marking the company first foldable smartphone and featuring John Ternus as CEO in the press release quote. item.title: Adobe Commerce max-severity bug comes under active attack
item.description:
Online stores running Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source face active attacks from a zero-day vulnerability tracked as C. V. E. twenty twenty-six, seventy-five thousand six hundred fifty.
The flaw carries a critical score of ten point zero and impacts versions two point four point four through two point four point nine of both platforms.
Security firm Sansec dubbed the flaw StyleSmuggler.
Exploitation began on September fourth, with the first confirmed attack recorded at twenty-two twenty U. T. C.
The vulnerability allows attackers to inject malicious P. H. P. code by abusing template processing during failed payment email notifications.
A successful attack launches a background process.
This process is a small Rust program that connects to a command and control server.
The server address is ninety-nine point eighty-four point sixty-seven point one hundred eighty-six.
The program waits for commands and uses persistence mechanisms like cron jobs.
It disguises its traffic as network time protocol traffic over U. D. P. port one hundred twenty-three.
A separate attacker used the vulnerability to deploy a web shell inside the product-image cache on September seventh.
Adobe released an emergency hotfix tracked as V. U. L. N. dash thirty-nine thousand three hundred forty-one to close the vulnerability.
Attackers had a three-day window to exploit the flaw before the fix arrived.
Sansec warns that patching alone is insufficient for stores that may have already been compromised.
Researchers recommend checking for unexpected P. H. P. files under pub slash media.
Stores should also look for known malicious processes, cron entries, and other indicators of compromise.

item.title: An Organizational Second Brain
item.description:
Meta has built an A. I. agent to act as a secondary expert for specific domains. It captures specialist knowledge that usually stays in human workers heads. The system saves domain experts substantial time in compliance workflows. It organizes institutional memory into a structured and auditable architecture. The design separates what the agent knows from how it reasons.
The system relies on four main layers. A knowledge system organizes over two hundred files into a strict taxonomy. This includes position files for authoritative stances and vocabulary files. It also uses routing indexes for deterministic retrieval and gateway files for threshold tests. Files use a format called Y. A. M. L. frontmatter to declare dependencies and consumers. This forms a bidirectional dependency graph. High-density and frequently referenced sources sit in this curated wiki. Sparse or situational sources are accessed through semantic or lexical search.
A reasoning layer uses composable procedures called recipes. These are imperative workflows that prescribe multi-step analysis without containing raw domain facts. This separation allows administrators to add organizational positions through knowledge files. They can do this without touching recipes. They can also fix analytical methodologies in recipes without changing knowledge files. This cuts token consumption per turn by around eighty percent.
Human oversight is maintained through checkpoints. The agent surfaces intermediate reasoning for review at these points. Escalations trigger when the agent encounters genuine ambiguity. Expert corrections and escalations feed an automated self-improvement loop. This loop compiles feedback into verified and regression-tested updates. It does all this without requiring model retraining. It turns one-off corrections into permanent institutional memory.

item.title: Rebuilding AUTOMATIC1111 with Gradio Workflow
item.description:
Workflow-one-one-one-one is a new graph-based implementation that rebuilds most of the feature set of AUTOMATIC-one-one-one-one's stable-diffusion-webui as a single workflow canvas using G. R. Workflow. The project demonstrates how Gradio Workflow covers similar functional ground to node graphs like Comfy-U. I. The canvas consists of seventy-three nodes and eleven media pipelines, bringing together state-of-the-art models for text-to-image, hi-resolution fix, image-to-image, prompt-matrix grids, V. L. M. interrogation, detection-to-inpaint masks, ControlNet-style annotators, background removal, P. N. G. Info storing, and image-to-video.
The application utilizes thirty-six operator nodes on the app, of which thirty-two are Python function nodes, with twenty-two running entirely in-process without a network call. You can run any of these pipelines by signing in with your Hugging Face account or providing an access token, which uses your own quota once you sign in. Every output node on the canvas automatically becomes a R. E. S. T. endpoint and an M. C. P. tool, exposing nine endpoints including image, edited image, generated prompt, recovered prompt, detected objects, x-y grid, upscaled local, annotator map, and p.n.g. info.
A node can be hardware you don't own, running through Inference Providers, any Space on the Hub, any A. P. I., or pulling from a dataset. The setup allows visitors to run workflows under their own identity using O. Auth, and mixes diffusion models, L. L. M.s, V. L. M.s, detectors, and video models on the same canvas.

item.title: ByteDance is Preparing a Real-Time Spatial Video Model
item.description:
ByteDance is preparing a new artificial intelligence model for real-time spatial video generation. Founder, Zhang Yiming, is personally overseeing the project. The launch could happen as soon as next month. A Bloomberg report cites unnamed sources for this news. One source cautions that the timing remains unsettled and plans could change. A ByteDance spokesperson did not respond to a request for comment.
The model is built on Seedance. That is the company existing video generation system. It allows users to create interactive virtual worlds for live streams and short-form dramas and games. Generation is handled in the cloud rather than locally on the device. This approach is intended to reduce the computational load and cost of extended reality hardware.
ByteDance owns the extended reality arm Pico. The new model generates virtual worlds that respond to Pico users voices and movements. Earlier reporting by, thirty-six Kr, indicated that ByteDance established world models as its top artificial intelligence priority for twenty twenty-six. This effort is backed by the company largest data budget. That budget is an eight-figure sum in renminbi. Sources describe it as three to four times rival spending. Capital expenditure considerations reach up to seventy billion dollars for its artificial intelligence build-out.

item.title: ClearFake WebDAV Infection Chain Delivers Amatera Stealer, ZigCryptoStealer, and NetSupport Manager
item.description:
Researchers at Cisco Talos investigated an unusual cyber attack at a Ukrainian government organization in April twenty twenty-six. The attack used a WebDAV execution chain. A thirty-two-bit rundll32.exe process launched a remote D. L. L. named verification.google.
One branch relied on a JavaScript injection. It used a Cloudflare Worker and EtherHiding on the B. N. B. Smart Chain. Victims were tricked into executing a WebDAV path through a fake Google CAPTCHA.
The resulting loader deployed Amatera build four point one point five alpha. This build found its command-and-control server through a Telegra.ph page disguised as a Rust tutorial. The server told the build to deploy a NativeAOT loader running ZigCryptoStealer and a Go-based reverse proxy.
The verification.google branch used a D. L. L. hollowing technique in dbghelp.dll. Its infrastructure instructed it to install an unauthorized instance of NetSupport Manager using a Russia-based I. P. address.
Cisco Talos tracks the threat actor behind the verification.google activity as U. A. T. dash ten thousand eight hundred twenty. They assess with moderate confidence that the operations are part of a broader crypto and credential theft network rather than targeted attacks against specific entities.

item.title: Reasoning Prefills on a Few Open Models, v1.1
item.description: The version one point one update to the reasoning prefill experiment uses G. P. T. five point five Pro as the teacher model to test open models. The evaluation consists of forty-five problems. These are split evenly into fifteen S. T. E. M. problems, fifteen non-S. T. E. M. problems, and fifteen synthetic puzzles. For each problem, the experiment generated two responses from each target model. One was an ordinary unprefilled response. The other started with the first one percent of G. P. T. five point five Pro's reasoning inserted into the target model's reasoning channel, while the visible answer remained freely generated. The author measured how much of the teacher's visible answer appeared in the first one hundred tokens of the target model's answer. Each score was calculated as the mean of unigram, bigram, and trigram source recall. Deltas were measured in absolute percentage point changes. Qwen, which barely moved toward Opus four point eight in the previous experiment, shifted by plus eighteen point one eight points toward G. P. T. five point five Pro. This showed a large effect on private synthetic puzzles. It suggests Qwen may have learned from G. P. T. five point five Pro or a closely related G. P. T. model rather than from Opus. Kimi K. three showed the highest overlap with G. P. T. five point five Pro both without and with the prefill. It recorded thirty-one point one one percent and thirty-five point six five percent respectively, though the prefill added only plus four point five four points.

item.title: Anthropic Models AI's Potential Impact on the US Economy
item.description: New research by the Anthropic Economics team models the economy using task bundles from the United States Department of Labor taxonomy, based on a technical report titled Economic Scenarios for Transformative AI. The study evaluates three futures based on artificial intelligence capabilities and adoption rates, and it includes an interactive scenario explorer tool. In the modest scenario, A I has an economic impact comparable to the internet, delivering gradual gains within historical norms. In the substantial scenario, A I performs half of all knowledge work by twenty thirty, with the majority done autonomously, driving the economy to grow at twice its normal rate. Unemployment rises to around five percent, gross domestic product sits ten percent higher than without A I, and wages for knowledge workers do not rise while other workers see gains. In the extreme scenario, driven by recursively self-improving systems, annual G D P growth reaches fifteen percent, doubling the economy every four point five years. This results in spiked unemployment and stagnating or declining wages for knowledge workers. A survey of more than ten thousand Americans conducted in August shows that the typical respondent expects the substantial change scenario. The model also indicates that labor and capital shares will shift, with capital demanding a larger percentage of total value compared to the historical baseline where workers receive about sixty cents of every dollar, against a backdrop of over thirty trillion dollars of value created over the past year in the United States economy. The study explores these shifts to provide visibility into the economic transition and ensure that benefits are broadly shared.

item.title: Congress-NC rift over Vande Mataram: The ghost of 1987 and ‘big brother’ complex
item.description: A disagreement over the song Vande Mataram has exposed a deeper power struggle between the National Conference and the Congress in Jammu and Kashmir. The dispute began Wednesday at the inaugural International Film Festival in Srinagar. National Conference leaders Omar Abdullah and Farooq Abdullah stood through the full three minute and ten second six stanza rendition of Vande Mataram in accordance with new central protocol. Congress leader Venugopal subsequently called on allies to honour the wisdom of freedom fighters. National Conference spokesperson, Tanvir Sadiq, clarified that the government was merely fulfilling a statutory obligation regardless of party ideology. This latest friction follows a series of uncoordinated moves and disagreements between the partners since the twenty twenty-four assembly elections restored their relationship. One such disagreement occurred in July twenty twenty-five when Congress announced uncoordinated protests demanding the restoration of Jammu and Kashmir statehood. In October twenty twenty-five, the allies deadlocked over four Rajya Sabha seats. The dominant National Conference initially discussed leaving one seat for Congress before disagreements arose over allocations. Omar Abdullah explained regarding the Rajya Sabha deadlock that they and Congress differed on winning chances. item.title: Expanding AI access and cyber defense for federal, state, local, and tribal governments
item.description:
OpenAI and the United States General Services Administration have announced a multi-year agreement. The deal expands artificial intelligence and cyber defense tools to federal, state, local, and tribal governments. The twenty-seven-month agreement runs from October first, twenty twenty-six, through December thirty-first, twenty twenty-eight. It extends eligibility across a public sector workforce of approximately twenty-three million people. This builds on existing agreements that already cover more than one million government employees.
The deal eliminates the standard fifteen-dollar-per-user-per-month license fee. It sets the fee to zero with no minimum commitment. It also provides fifty percent off usage costs for eligible organizations. Verified government entities will be approved for advanced cyber-defender Daybreak Blue access. This comes at fifty percent off standard commercial pricing alongside scaled training and enablement. Defenders can also request access to Daybreak Red. This tool offers advanced vulnerability research, exploit validation, and red teaming at standard commercial pricing.
Practical implementations under previous access show major successes. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention accelerated public health literature reviews to under thirty minutes. The Georgia Department of Revenue reduced tax form digitization time from two weeks to fifteen minutes. The North Carolina Department of State Treasurer identified millions of dollars in potential unclaimed property. Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory compressed months of fusion research model development into hours. OpenAI President, Greg Brockman, stated that public servants should have access to the best A. I. tools available. He noted that helping government work better by making services faster, easier, safer, and more reliable is a key way to bring the benefits of A. I. to everyone.

item.title: Introducing ChatGPT for Financial Services
item.description:
OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT for Financial Services. It is a tailored work experience combining built-in financial data with G. P. T. dash six Astra reasoning. item.title: The Download: a “God-driven” cryptocurrency and a solar engineering roadmap
item.description:
Apple has officially entered the foldable phone market. The company announced a new device called the iPhone Duo. It will cost one thousand nine hundred ninety-nine dollars. item.title: Shopify is moving from React Native back to Swift and Kotlin
item.description:
Shopify is moving its mobile technology stack from React Native back to native Swift and Kotlin. The company cites advancements in coding models and artificial intelligence agents that have removed the historic cost of building features twice. Shopify originally adopted React Native in twenty twenty to streamline development. Modern large language models now allow agents to handle implementation, translation, testing, and review work across platforms.
To manage the migration, Shopify built a system called Helix. This system breaks work into small, reviewed checkpoints requiring tests and human sign off. The company also developed a command line interface architecture that decouples business logic from the user interface. This lets agents test and iterate in milliseconds instead of using slow mobile simulators.
The Shop app is the first of Shopify applications to complete the migration to native Swift and Kotlin. It was fully rebuilt and published in the app stores using this artificial intelligence assisted approach in just twelve weeks. Migration of the larger Shopify app includes over three hundred screens. That migration is underway and scheduled to ship later this year. It will be followed by remaining apps like Point of Sale and Inbox.
As part of the transition, Shopify will continue sponsoring its open source library FlashList through the end of twenty twenty-six. FlashList draws roughly two million downloads a week. Shopify is discussing long term stewardship with other companies and planning for a fork managed by, William Candillon. The Restyle library will also be supported through the end of twenty twenty-six before its repository is archived.

item.title: The Four-Color Theorem Gets a Rare New Proof
item.description:
A team of six mathematicians from Denmark, Canada, and Japan has produced a new proof of the four-color theorem.
Any map can be colored using only four colors without adjacent regions sharing a color.
The researchers worked for nearly a decade.
They posted their findings online in March twenty twenty-six.
They will present the work in November at the annual Foundations of Computer Science conference.
Previous proofs from nineteen seventy-six and nineteen ninety-seven required sequential steps proportional to $n$ squared.
That applied to a graph with $n$ vertices.
The new proof identifies an unavoidable set of eight thousand two hundred and two configurations in flat areas of graphs.
These configurations can be reduced at the same time.
This drops the coloring process to $n$ times the log of $n$ steps.
The team drew on a different concept of reducibility.
They used overlooked parts of the graph.
The work has revealed previously unknown structure in these important mathematical objects.
The findings provide mathematicians with new tools for solving other stubborn problems in graph theory.
Georges Gonthier, of Inria in Paris, noted the team used an intricate approach.
He stated it is really cool to see a real result for once.
He mentioned the problem has a history of false starts and dashed hopes.

item.title: Now everyone can put data to work
item.description:
OpenAI is introducing a new Data agent in ChatGPT Work. This tool lets employees query company data and build interactive dashboards using plain language. Users do not need to write code or learn new analytics tools.
